correctness.rationale: Each decoded bit factors through the intersection quotient induced by its disjoint recovery-set column spans; rank counting gives quotient dimension at most floor(r/(t-1)). For r<=3t-4 this is at most two, where balanced binary functions are affine. Bijectivity then makes the full labeling affine and yields a linear encoder with the same recovery sets.

originality.rationale: The primary nonlinear 3-PIR source explicitly distinguishes nonlinear labeling of a linear associated code from a nonlinear associated code but does not give this low-redundancy reduction. Searches across exact and synonymous formulations and later PIR/batch literature found no equivalent theorem. Originality is to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The theorem eliminates nonlinear labeling as a source of advantage throughout a natural low-redundancy range and proves that any solution to the documented open binary 3-PIR parameter (n,k)=(11,7) must use a genuinely nonlinear associated code.
